svg.text: Codillon checks that every return path lands in Gcd(a, b)
Per-instruction dependent fiber display: the loop preserves Gcd(x, y) = Gcd(a, b); a bad return is caught visually
Codillon Structured Wasm: fn euclid(a: ℕ, b: ℕ) → Gcd(a, b)
Target Return Fiber: Gcd(a, b) = { g ∈ ℕ | Div(g) = Div(a) ∩ Div(b) }
Probe: (a=12, b=8) ⇒ target fiber {4} | symbolic g* in indigo
branch guard refines type of y:
x ∈ Gcd(x, 0) = Gcd(x, y) = Gcd(a, b)
TYPE ERROR: {0} ≠ Gcd(a, b) for a∨b > 0
preserves Div(y) ∩ Div(x mod y) = Div(x) ∩ Div(y)
Gcd(y, x mod y) = Gcd(x, y) = Gcd(a, b)
Symbolic Fiber Verification (All Inputs a, b)
Indigo marks unknown symbolic value g*; refinement proves fibers coincide
Even with g* unknown (indigo), Codillon proves Gcd(x,0) = {x} = Gcd(a,b)!
Live Fiber Target Check in Codillon Gutter
Comparing well-typed `return x` vs. ill-typed `return y` at loop exit (y = 0):
Case 1: Inputs (a = 12, b = 8) → Target Fiber Gcd(12, 8) = {4}
Case 2: Boundary Input (a = 21, b = 0) → Target Fiber Gcd(21, 0) = {21}
Runtime evidence is erased: only the plain integer 4 (or 21) flows on the Wasm stack.
